questions.stem: HEAT transfer by the movement of molecules in a FLUID (liquid or gas) is called:
questions.explanation: THREE MODES of HEAT TRANSFER: (1) CONDUCTION — heat flows through direct molecular contact in a SOLID (or between touching objects); hot particles vibrate faster → transfer energy to adjacent particles. Good conductors: metals (Cu, Ag, Al — sea of free electrons), diamond. Poor conductors (insulators): wood, plastic, air, wool, silica aerogel. (2) CONVECTION — in FLUIDS (liquids + gases): heated fluid EXPANDS, becomes LESS DENSE, RISES; cooler fluid sinks. Natural convection — no pump (sea breezes, hot air balloons, boiling water). Forced convection — pumps + fans (car radiator, central heating). Drives OCEAN CURRENTS (thermohaline circulation), atmospheric winds (Hadley cells), weather systems. Cannot happen in VACUUM or SOLIDS. (3) RADIATION — transfer via ELECTROMAGNETIC WAVES (infrared); NO medium required — works in VACUUM; Sun's energy reaches Earth via radiation across 150 million km. Described by STEFAN-BOLTZMANN LAW: P = σAT⁴ (A = area, T = absolute temperature, σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W/m²K⁴). BLACK BODY radiates most; shiny SILVER radiates least. KIRCHHOFF'S law: good absorbers are good emitters. THERMOS FLASK uses all three controls — double-walled silvered vacuum flask: vacuum stops conduction + convection; silver coating reflects radiation. EXAMPLES: conduction = touching a hot pan; convection = boiling water; radiation = warming under the Sun. Why clothes are black in winter (absorb more Sun radiation)/white in summer (reflect). hot fluid rises (less dense), cool fluid sinks; drives sea breezes, weather, boiling water.

questions.stem: The FIRST LAW of THERMODYNAMICS states that:

options.option_text: Entropy of an isolated system never decreases
ENERGY can neither be CREATED nor DESTROYED, only converted from one form to another
Two bodies in thermal equilibrium have equal temperatures

questions.explanation: FIRST LAW of THERMODYNAMICS = Law of CONSERVATION OF ENERGY applied to thermodynamic systems. Formulation: ΔU = Q − W; where ΔU = change in internal energy; Q = heat added TO the system; W = work done BY the system. Energy is neither created nor destroyed — only transformed. EXAMPLES: (a) heat given to gas → raises internal energy + does work (pushing piston); (b) mechanical work done on gas → raises internal energy (compression heats gas — diesel engine ignition); (c) electrical energy → heat (resistance heater); → light + sound (speakers + LEDs). HISTORICAL: formulated by James Prescott JOULE (1843-1847 paddle-wheel experiment showing mechanical work ≡ heat; mechanical equivalent of heat ~4.18 J/cal); ROBERT MAYER, HERMANN HELMHOLTZ, RUDOLF CLAUSIUS (~1850). DEBUNKED perpetual motion MACHINE of the FIRST KIND (gives more energy output than input — impossible). RELATED LAWS: (a) ZEROTH LAW — if A ≡ B thermally + B ≡ C, then A ≡ C (defines temperature); formulated later but numbered 'zero' so it's logically prior. (b) SECOND LAW — entropy of isolated system never decreases (time's arrow, Clausius/Kelvin — no heat engine converts 100% heat to work, no refrigerator works with no input; MAX EFFICIENCY = Carnot = 1 − Tc/Th). (c) THIRD LAW — absolute zero unattainable (Walther Nernst, 1906). Second law is why HEAT ENGINES (IC engines, turbines) have efficiency <100% — the 'Carnot limit' in a steam turbine: η = 1 − Tcold/Thot; boiler 900K, condenser 300K → Carnot η ≈ 66%, actual ~35%.

_fixes.was: ENERGY can neither be CREATED nor DESTROYED, only converted from one form to another (ΔU = Q − W)
_fixes.now: ENERGY can neither be CREATED nor DESTROYED, only converted from one form to another

questions.stem: The temperature at which a liquid CHANGES to VAPOUR at atmospheric pressure is called its:
questions.explanation: BOILING POINT — temperature at which the VAPOUR PRESSURE of a liquid EQUALS the external (atmospheric) pressure, allowing BUBBLES to form throughout the liquid. For WATER at 1 atm = 100°C = 373.15 K = 212°F. LOWERED at HIGH ALTITUDE: (a) Darjeeling/Shimla (~2000 m) water boils at ~93°C; (b) Mt Everest summit (8848 m) ~72°C — can't cook rice/dal properly; (c) solution: PRESSURE COOKER (raises pressure → higher boiling point → faster cooking). On Everest, pressure cooker is essential. At 2 atm, water boils at ~120°C. CONVERSELY, pure distilled water in open container can BOIL AT ROOM TEMPERATURE in vacuum chamber. MELTING POINT — solid-to-liquid transition; for ice = 0°C at 1 atm. FREEZING POINT same as melting point for pure substances. DEW POINT — temperature at which water vapour in air begins to condense; humidity indicator. LATENT HEAT: extra heat needed to cause PHASE CHANGE without temperature change. (a) Latent heat of fusion of ice = 80 cal/g (or 334 kJ/kg); (b) latent heat of vaporisation of water = 540 cal/g (or 2260 kJ/kg) — very high, which is why SWEATING cools us efficiently (evaporation takes a lot of heat from skin). SPECIFIC HEAT CAPACITY: water = 4186 J/kg·K — very HIGH (why coastal climates are moderate, water heats/cools slowly); iron = 450; air = 1005. Water's anomalous expansion: densest at 4°C (why ice floats, lakes freeze from top, aquatic life survives winter). for water, 100 °C at 1 atm.

questions.stem: A thermos flask prevents heat loss primarily through:

options.option_text: A VACUUM between double walls (stops conduction + convection) + silvered surfaces

questions.explanation: THERMOS FLASK — or VACUUM FLASK, invented by SIR JAMES DEWAR (1892) for cryogenic experiments; commercialised by THERMOS GmbH (Berlin, 1904). DESIGN: double-walled glass or metal bottle with: (1) VACUUM between the two walls — eliminates CONDUCTION (no matter to conduct) + CONVECTION (no fluid to circulate). (2) SILVERED inner + outer surfaces of the double wall — REFLECT thermal INFRARED radiation back to the contents (minimising radiation loss). (3) CORK/plastic stopper with low thermal conductivity — reduces heat escape through the top. (4) Outer plastic/metal casing — protects the fragile vacuum wall from impact. PERFORMANCE: good flask keeps hot drinks ~70°C after 12 hours; cold drinks near 4°C for a day. EVERYDAY variants: Camper's Hydro Flask, Milton, Cello, Milton Thermosteel, Eagle (Indian brands). SAME PRINCIPLE used in: (a) cryogenic Dewars for liquid nitrogen (-196°C) + liquid helium (-269°C); (b) space telescope insulation (JWST); (c) insulation for LNG tankers. THERMODYNAMIC CONCEPT: near-perfect ISOLATED SYSTEM — no heat exchange with surroundings; a familiar toy example of adiabatic containment. ESCAPE ROUTES even in a perfect thermos: (a) residual gas in imperfect vacuum; (b) thin glass/metal thermal bridge at the seal; (c) radiation if silvering degraded. GLASS VACUUM flasks DANGEROUS if broken — implode. Modern STAINLESS STEEL vacuum flasks safer. reflects radiation.

_fixes.was: A VACUUM between double walls (stops conduction + convection) + silvered surfaces (reflects radiation)
_fixes.now: A VACUUM between double walls (stops conduction + convection) + silvered surfaces

questions.stem: The 'LATENT HEAT of FUSION' of ICE is:
questions.explanation: LATENT HEAT — heat absorbed or released during a PHASE CHANGE at constant temperature. For WATER: (a) LATENT HEAT OF FUSION (ice → water) = ~80 CAL/G = 334 J/g = 334 kJ/kg at 0°C. (b) LATENT HEAT OF VAPORISATION (water → steam) = 540 cal/g = 2260 J/g = 2260 kJ/kg at 100°C. (c) Latent heat of sublimation (ice → steam directly) = sum of both ~620 cal/g. PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCES: (1) Ice cools drinks VERY efficiently — even after it reaches 0°C, it needs 80 cal/g to MELT, absorbing lots of heat from the drink. (2) COOLING by EVAPORATION — sweat needs ~540 cal/g to evaporate from skin — massive cooling effect. Why fans feel cool (enhance evaporation). Why desert coolers work (dry air takes up moisture + cools by vaporisation). (3) STEAM BURNS WORSE than hot water burns at same temperature — when 100°C steam condenses on skin, it releases 540 cal/g of latent heat ON TOP of cooling from 100°C to body temp. (4) CLOUDS forming release latent heat → warm atmosphere + drive convection, hurricanes, thunderstorms. (5) AIR CONDITIONERS + refrigerators USE latent heat — refrigerant evaporates in the cold coil (absorbs heat from room), condenses in the hot coil outside (releases heat). CALCULATIONS: melting 1 kg ice at 0°C → 1 kg water at 0°C needs 334 kJ; heating 1 kg water from 0→100°C needs 4186 × 100 = 418.6 kJ; boiling 1 kg water at 100°C to steam needs 2260 kJ. Total for 1 kg ice → steam = 334 + 418.6 + 2260 ≈ 3013 kJ. heat required to melt 1 gram of ice at 0°C without changing temperature.

_fixes.was: 80 cal/g (334 kJ/kg) — heat required to melt 1 gram of ice at 0°C without changing temperature

questions.stem: WATER reaches its MAXIMUM DENSITY at:
questions.explanation: WATER'S ANOMALOUS EXPANSION — unlike most substances, water's DENSITY does NOT monotonically increase as temperature drops. Between 4°C and 0°C water EXPANDS (density decreases) as it cools. DENSITY: peaks at ~1.000 g/cm³ at 4°C; drops to ~0.9998 at 0°C (liquid); drops abruptly to ~0.917 at 0°C (solid ice). So ICE is LIGHTER than cold water → FLOATS. REASON: WATER MOLECULES form HYDROGEN BONDS via their polar O-H bonds. In solid ice, molecules arrange in an OPEN HEXAGONAL lattice with large gaps (required by H-bond geometry) → lower density. Below 4°C, clusters of tetrahedral 'ice-like' structures start to form in the liquid, expanding it. Above 4°C, normal thermal expansion dominates. CONSEQUENCES — CRUCIAL FOR LIFE: (1) LAKES + RIVERS freeze TOP-DOWN: cold water at 4°C sinks + stays at bottom (densest); water at 0°C floats up + freezes as ICE on surface. The ice layer INSULATES the liquid beneath, keeping it at 4°C → AQUATIC LIFE SURVIVES winter. Without this anomaly, lakes would freeze SOLID bottom-up → aquatic life would die + climate would be very different. (2) FROST DAMAGE to crops + pipes: water expands ~9% on freezing → bursts pipes, cracks rocks, shatters ceramics. (3) GLACIERS + ICEBERGS float on seas → ~90% underwater (hence 'tip of the iceberg'). (4) Drops of water freeze + expand in plant cells → killing tropical crops. Agricultural relevance: frost-tolerance breeding; chilling injury. OTHER anomalous liquids: bismuth, antimony, silicon, gallium all EXPAND on freezing. Most substances contract on cooling + expand on heating. ANOMALOUS expansion; below 4°C water EXPANDS as it cools; why ice floats + lakes freeze from top down.

questions.stem: A BIMETALLIC STRIP (used in thermostats + fire alarms) works because:

options.option_text: DIFFERENT metals EXPAND BY DIFFERENT AMOUNTS when heated, causing the strip to BEND

questions.explanation: BIMETALLIC STRIP — two strips of different metals (usually BRASS + INVAR, or BRASS + IRON, or COPPER + STEEL) riveted together along their length. When heated, the two metals expand at DIFFERENT RATES (different LINEAR EXPANSION COEFFICIENTS α). The strip bends TOWARDS the LOW-EXPANSION metal. Typical α values: brass = 19 × 10⁻⁶ /K; iron = 12 × 10⁻⁶ /K; invar (Fe-Ni alloy) = 1.2 × 10⁻⁶ /K (invented by Guillaume 1896, Nobel 1920). USES: (1) THERMOSTATS in electric irons, geysers, ovens, refrigerators, AC units — the bend breaks/makes an electrical contact at the set temperature. (2) FIRE ALARMS — strip bends at high temp → closes the alarm circuit. (3) MECHANICAL CLOCK compensation for temperature drift. (4) Bimetallic THERMOMETERS (dial type). LINEAR EXPANSION: ΔL = L₀ × α × ΔT. AREA expansion coefficient = 2α; VOLUME expansion coefficient = 3α. WHY EXPANSION: increased temperature → atoms vibrate with larger amplitude → average inter-atomic distance increases slightly → solid grows. In engineering: EXPANSION JOINTS in bridges (steel expands ~1 cm per 10m per 50°C change), railway tracks (gap between rails — 'clickety-clack'), pipelines, concrete slabs — all accommodate thermal expansion. Hot-water bottles / overhead wires sag in summer + taut in winter. INVAR: designed for NIL expansion → precision instruments, watches, aircraft + space; Superinvar (Fe-Ni-Co) has even less. SPECIAL: water between 0-4°C has NEGATIVE volume expansion coefficient. closing/opening an electrical circuit.

questions.stem: THIRD LAW of THERMODYNAMICS states that:

options.option_text: Absolute ZERO (0 K = −273.15 °C) cannot be REACHED by any finite number of operations
Heat flows from hot to cold

questions.explanation: THIRD LAW OF THERMODYNAMICS — formulated by WALTHER NERNST (1906; Nobel 1920). Two equivalent statements: (a) Entropy S of a PERFECT CRYSTAL at ABSOLUTE ZERO (0 K) is EXACTLY ZERO (minimum, unique configuration). (b) Absolute zero is UNATTAINABLE — can only approach asymptotically; each successive reduction in temperature takes more energy than the previous. COLDEST temperatures achieved: (a) Vostok, Antarctica NATURAL record: −89.2°C (surface, 1983); (b) DOMA Ridge, Antarctica: −98°C (from satellite, 2018). (c) LAB: Bose-Einstein condensates cooled to ~38 pK (picokelvin = 10⁻¹² K) — MIT + Leiden experiments. Nanokelvin in atomic magnetometers + quantum computers. DEEP SPACE: cosmic microwave background ~2.725 K. BOOMERANG NEBULA (5000 ly away) ~1 K — coldest known NATURAL place due to rapid adiabatic expansion from dying star. (Lower than CMB!). IMPLICATIONS: (1) HEAT ENGINES: Kelvin-Planck statement of 2nd law implies no engine has 100% efficiency; Carnot η = 1 − Tc/Th; only at Tc = 0 K could η = 100% — but 3rd law forbids it. Universe never gives us absolute-zero sinks. (2) QUANTUM mechanics: as T→0, particles don't come to rest — ZERO-POINT ENERGY remains (a quantum effect — Heisenberg uncertainty requires residual motion). (3) Superconductivity, superfluidity, Bose-Einstein + Fermi condensation all occur near absolute zero. Chemistry: standard entropies tabulated starting from S(0K) = 0. Astrobiology: habitable zone of planets sensitive to lower bound of liquid water. entropy of a perfect crystal at 0 K equals zero.

questions.stem: The LARGE specific heat capacity of water (~4186 J/kg·K) is responsible for:

options.option_text: MODERATING climate near large water bodies

questions.explanation: SPECIFIC HEAT CAPACITY (c) — heat needed to raise 1 kg of a substance by 1 K (or 1°C). WATER'S c = 4186 J/(kg·K) = 1 cal/(g·K) = 4.186 kJ/(kg·K) — EXCEPTIONALLY HIGH (2nd highest of common substances, after liquid ammonia). REASON for high c of water: H-bonds take lots of energy to partially break as water heats up. CONSEQUENCES + applications: (1) CLIMATE MODERATION: oceans absorb heat in summer + release slowly in winter → COASTAL climates are milder (Mumbai, Chennai vs Nagpur). Ocean acts as thermal buffer for the planet — slows global warming (oceans absorbed ~90% of excess heat from CO₂ forcing). (2) COOLANT in engineering: car RADIATORS use water to absorb engine heat without boiling; nuclear reactor cooling; industrial chillers. (3) HOT WATER BOTTLE keeps warm longer than any other common substance. (4) COOKING slow with water — takes time to heat; good for even cooking of rice, dal. (5) HUMAN BODY is ~60% water — buffers body temperature despite metabolic heat generation; sweating (evaporation) cools us. (6) STEAM heating systems in buildings + industry. COMPARISON: specific heats (J/kg·K): water 4186; ice 2100; steam 2010; air 1005; aluminium 900; iron 450; copper 385; gold 128; lead 128; sand 830; marble 880; glass 840; ethanol 2420; sea water 3850 (slightly less due to salts). Good DELETE cooling fluid choice depends on both specific heat + boiling point + viscosity + corrosion. slow heating + slow cooling of oceans; why coastal cities have less extreme temperatures than inland.

questions.stem: A PRESSURE COOKER cooks FASTER than an open pot because:

options.option_text: Higher pressure inside RAISES the BOILING POINT of water to ~120 °C, so food cooks faster at higher temperature

questions.explanation: PRESSURE COOKER — exploits the fact that BOILING POINT RISES WITH PRESSURE. Standard atmospheric pressure = 1 atm (101.325 kPa); water boils at 100°C. Pressure cookers operate at ~1.5-2 atm (gauge pressure 15 psi on top of 1 atm atmospheric). This raises water's boiling point to ~120°C — which: (a) cooks food ~3× FASTER (chemical reaction rate roughly doubles for every 10°C rise, Q10 rule, Arrhenius equation); (b) makes tough meats + dal tender faster; (c) reduces fuel + time consumption ~40-70%. INVENTED by FRENCH physicist DENIS PAPIN (1679) — his 'steam digester' / 'Digester of Bones'. SAFETY: (a) WEIGHTED VALVE on lid whistles at set pressure — excess steam escapes; (b) SAFETY FUSE (rubber or metal) melts / ruptures at emergency overpressure preventing explosion; (c) GASKET seals the lid; replace if torn. HIGH-ALTITUDE cooking: essential above 2000m where boiling point drops below 95°C + food barely cooks; Himalayan treks always use pressure cookers. OTHER applications of pressure-boiling relation: (1) autoclaves (medical sterilisers) — 121°C at 15 psi for 15 min kills heat-resistant spores. (2) Retort pouches + canning — high temp under pressure sterilises food. (3) Geyser (hot spring) water often exceeds 100°C underground due to overlying rock pressure; flashes to steam when pressure drops on surface (e.g., Yellowstone geysers). REVERSE: water in VACUUM boils at room temperature → used in vacuum distillation (alcohol manufacture, pharma). 'ENGINEERING TOILET BRAIN HACK': Le Chatelier's principle — increased pressure shifts vapor-liquid equilibrium toward liquid phase, requiring higher T to boil.
